intro: Houston mixes world-class museums, NASA history and a food scene built on immigration. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: METRORail light rail covers about 37 km on Red, Green and Purple lines.
METRO buses fill the gaps; fare is about $1.25 each way.
Pay with a METRO Q Card or day pass for free transfers within 3 hours.
Uber and Lyft are widely used; Empower is a local lower-cost option.
Driving is easiest but rush hour runs roughly 7-9AM and 4-6:30PM.
Downtown is walkable; elsewhere sidewalks are patchy and heat is fierce.

space-center.name: Space Center Houston
space-center.price_text: ≈ USD 30–40 adult · child and senior rates lower · check online for current price
space-center.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–17:00 · check on the day for closures
space-center.tip: Book online and arrive at opening. The tram tour to the historic Mission Control is the highlight and fills up fast.

houston-zoo.name: Houston Zoo
houston-zoo.price_text: ≈ USD 20–35 adult depending on date · buy online
houston-zoo.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
houston-zoo.tip: Go early in the morning. Houston heat peaks midday, and the animals are more active before it.

downtown-aquarium.name: Downtown Aquarium
downtown-aquarium.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–20:00 · check on the day
downtown-aquarium.tip: Good for families and a rainy afternoon. The upstairs restaurant has tanks around the tables.

rice-university.name: Rice University
rice-university.hours: Campus grounds generally open daily · buildings vary
rice-university.tip: Walk the live-oak quad and the Moody Center for the Arts. It is a calm break from the museum crowds.

funplex.name: Funplex
funplex.price_text: Pay per ride or attraction · check current prices on site
funplex.hours: Check on the day · hours vary by season
funplex.tip: A family fun park with rides and games. Confirm opening hours before you drive out; it is far from downtown.

hermann-park.name: Hermann Park
hermann-park.price_text: Free · paddle boats and train cost extra
hermann-park.tip: Rent a paddle boat on the lake or ride the small train. Shade is limited, so bring water.

museum-fine-arts.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
museum-fine-arts.price_text: ≈ USD 15–25 adult · free on some days, check online
museum-fine-arts.hours: Closed Monday · otherwise roughly 11:00–17:00, later some days
museum-fine-arts.tip: Big collection across two buildings. Check the free-admission day before you go.

natural-science-museum.name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
natural-science-museum.price_text: ≈ USD 20–30 permanent exhibits · planetarium and butterfly house extra
natural-science-museum.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
natural-science-museum.tip: The dinosaur hall and butterfly center suit all ages. Buy timed tickets online to skip lines.

buffalo-bayou.name: Buffalo Bayou Park and hike-and-bike trail
buffalo-bayou.hours: Trails open daily, dawn to dusk
buffalo-bayou.tip: Walk or rent a bike along the bayou. The skyline view from the west end is best near sunset.

market-square.name: Market Square Park and historic district
market-square.price_text: Free to enter · food and drink extra
market-square.hours: Park daily · nearby bars and cafes vary
market-square.tip: A small downtown park with bars around it. Good stop on a downtown walk in the evening.

montrose-walk.name: Westheimer Road in Montrose
montrose-walk.price_text: Free to walk · cafes and shops extra
montrose-walk.hours: Shops and cafes vary · liveliest afternoon to late evening
montrose-walk.tip: Walk Westheimer for cafes, vintage shops and restaurants. It is Houston's most walkable strip.

galleria.name: The Galleria
galleria.price_text: Free to enter · shopping and ice rink extra
galleria.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–20:00 · check on the day
galleria.tip: A huge mall with an indoor ice rink. Handy on a hot or rainy day.

food-hall-downtown.name: Downtown food hall and Finn Hall area
food-hall-downtown.price_text: Meals roughly USD 10–20 · check on the day
food-hall-downtown.tip: Many small vendors under one roof. Good for groups who want different food.

tunnel-walk.name: Downtown tunnel walk
tunnel-walk.tip: An underground network of shops and food courts. It is air-conditioned and busy at lunch.

waterwall.name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
waterwall.tip: A tall curved water wall near the Galleria. A quick photo stop, best in cooler hours.

menil.name: The Menil Collection
menil.hours: Closed Monday and Tuesday · otherwise roughly 11:00–19:00
menil.tip: A free art museum in a leafy neighbourhood. Combine it with a walk to the nearby Rothko Chapel.

rothko-chapel.name: Rothko Chapel
rothko-chapel.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
rothko-chapel.tip: A quiet space for reflection. Keep voices low and skip it if you want lively sightseeing.

city-tour.name: Houston city sightseeing tour
city-tour.price_text: ≈ USD 30–60 depending on operator and length
city-tour.tip: A bus or van tour is an easy way to see the spread-out city without driving. Confirm pickup point.

sabercat-statue.name: Houston Sabercats and stadium area walk
sabercat-statue.price_text: Event tickets vary · check on the day
sabercat-statue.tip: Check the sports calendar if you want a game. Otherwise skip this area.

kemah.name: Kemah Boardwalk day trip
kemah.price_text: Free to walk · rides and restaurants extra
kemah.hours: Rides and shops vary · check on the day
kemah.tip: A waterfront boardwalk with rides and seafood, about an hour from downtown. Go for sunset.

bbq-stop.name: Classic Texas barbecue lunch
bbq-stop.price_text: ≈ USD 15–35 per person · check on the day
bbq-stop.hours: Often lunch only or until sold out · check on the day
bbq-stop.tip: Houston barbecue is a must. Go early; popular spots sell out by mid-afternoon.

stays.why: Walkable core near the theater district, sports arenas and the rail line; good base without a car.
Quiet, leafy and next to the big museums, Hermann Park and the zoo; easy rail to downtown.
Mall shopping, many restaurants and hotels; handy if you plan to drive or shop.
Bars, cafés and galleries; central for nightlife and close to the Museum District.

food: Try Texas barbecue: brisket and ribs by the pound. Popular spots get long lines; go early or off-peak.
Tex-Mex is the local staple: breakfast tacos, fajitas and queso. Expect $8–15 for a plate.
Look for Viet-Cajun crawfish in season (roughly spring). Prices vary by market; check on the day.
Montrose and the Heights have dense clusters of cafés and casual restaurants; walk and pick one.
Tipping is expected: about 15–20% at sit-down restaurants.
more_time: Add a beach day at Galveston, about an hour's drive southeast; check traffic and the weather first.
Museum lovers can spend a half day at the Museum of Fine Arts and the nearby Hermann Park.
Baseball or basketball fans: check the Astros and Rockets home schedules before booking.
